gaps.sentence: Never before that afternoon ___ so many goals been scored in one match.
gaps.explanation: 'Never before that afternoon' fixes the reference in the past: had so many goals been scored.

gaps.sentence: Only after the interview ___ I realise how nervous I had been.
gaps.explanation: Only after X did I realise… — inversion.

gaps.sentence: We had no ___ signed the lease than the landlord sold the building.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner … than' — here with 'had' before the participle.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ anyone noticed the subtle change in the final scene.
Seldom have I been so ___ by a performance.
gaps.explanation: 'moved' — the audience was emotionally affected; inversion with have been.

gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ his argument that nobody objected.
gaps.explanation: So + adjective at the front: was his argument that…

gaps.sentence: On no account ___ passengers open this door.
gaps.explanation: On no account should passengers… — formal prohibition.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.
